#### 1. STING-associated vasculopathy with onset in infancy  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.473)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9705671)

Mutations in CNBP lead to autosomal dominant centronuclear myopathy (Disease A). Gain-of-function mutations in STING1 lead to constitutive activation of type I interferon production, resulting in vasculitis with infantile onset (Disease B). The shared convergence is on the STING1 pathway, which, while dysregulated in Disease B, may also be indirectly affected by broader cellular dysfunction in Disease A, or represent a parallel pathway contributing to inflammatory phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a specific variant in STING1 with a documented loss-of-function effect in patients with STING-associated vasculopathy with onset in infancy, or absence of any shared downstream signaling pathway activation between the two diseases in cellular models. _(variant: rs113812168)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared involvement of the STING1 pathway, even with divergent functional consequences, could reveal novel therapeutic targets for inflammatory manifestations present in both conditions or related disorders. The convergence is on the NF-kappaB pathway, which is a central regulator of immune responses and also implicated in cellular processes that could indirectly affect neuronal function.

**How to falsify it:** The demonstration that mutations in CNBP do not affect RNA processing or lead to intellectual disability, or that mutations in IKBKB do not impact NF-kappaB signaling or cause immunodeficiency. _(variant: Presence of pathogenic CNBP or IKBKB variants in gnomAD with allele frequencies significantly higher than expected for rare diseases.)_
